title: fix(service-analytics): log the admitObjectRead bridge's init-time security absence at info; WARN once at the first query that finds none
body:
Fixes #22154

Clause-②: no

## What changed

`packages/services/service-analytics/src/plugin.ts`, the `admitObjectRead` bridge's absence logging only:

- **Init-time line: `warn` to `info`**, the same level and shape the sibling `getReadScope` line already uses for the identical situation: `[Analytics] admitObjectRead bridged to the "security" service; that service is not registered yet at init and will be resolved per query (plugin order is not significant).`
- **Per-query bridge, ABSENT branch** (the plugin context answers a lookup for `security` with nothing): it still returns `true` (admit), exactly as before, and now logs ONE WARN at the first query that finds no service, naming that query's object: `[Analytics] No admitObjectRead configured and no "security" service registered when an analytics query needed one (first: "OBJECT") ...`. Once per plugin instance: a closure flag created per `init()`, deliberately not a module binding, so a second kernel in the same process gets its own report. The flag records only that the report was made; it caches no verdict, and every query still resolves the service afresh.
- The UNUSABLE branch (lookup threw, or the service answers neither `canReadObject` nor `explain`), the `getReadScope` bridge, and the `translateSelectOptions` region are untouched.

Tests (all in `service-analytics`): new `src/__tests__/admission-absence-report.test.ts` (5 cases); `raw-sql-object-routing.test.ts` follows the moved WARN text; `admission-bridge-resolution.test.ts` header comment. One `@objectstack/service-analytics` `patch` changeset.

## Why the init-time WARN was always false on a default boot (measured)

`@objectstack/plugin-security` registers the `security` service in its `start()`: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts:2355`, inside `start()` (opens at `:1646`; `init()` opens at `:1461`). So at analytics' `init()` that service can never be present on a composition that ships plugin-security, whatever the plugin order, and the old branch fired on every default boot.

## PM mechanism hypotheses, measured

- **H1, confirmed** at `7d7943dd`: the init-time line was `ctx.logger.warn` at `plugin.ts:1449`; the `getReadScope` sibling logs at `info` at `:1430`; the `admitObjectRead` closure built at `:754` calls `trySecurityAdmission()` (`ctx.getService('security')`) on every call.
- **H2, refined.** What the per-query bridge does today when no security service resolves depends on how the context answers the miss:
  - a context whose `getService` returns nothing (every in-package test double): the ABSENT branch admits and, before this PR, logged nothing;
  - the in-repo kernels (`ObjectKernel`, `LiteKernel`) THROW on a never-registered name (`[Kernel] Service 'security' not found`), so the bridge takes the UNUSABLE branch: every query is DENIED `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403 with an `error` line per query, and nothing is read.
  - This PR keeps both outcomes exactly. On the in-repo kernels, absence at query time was and stays loud at `error`; the new once-WARN lives in the ABSENT branch. The divergence between the two classifications is reported to the seat as a separate finding; it is not changed here.
- **H3, green, with a caveat.** `pnpm check:startup-registry-verdict` and `pnpm check:init-service-contract` are green on this head. The startup-registry gate is ALSO green on the pre-fix tree, and it lists the analytics `security` probe as `read-only (legal) [final: no workspace plugin declares providesServices: ['security']]` both before and after. It does not see this shape, because `providesServices` is init-only by contract and plugin-security registers `security` in `start()`. Its green is not evidence for or against this fix.
- **H4, pinned and ablated** (below).

## Before / after, real kernels, built `dist`

A scratch probe booted a real kernel with a `data` provider and this plugin, plus optionally a security provider registered after analytics' init, and ran the same dataset query twice. Rows below are admission-related log lines and outcomes.

| kernel, security | before (`7d7943dd`) | after (this head) |
|---|---|---|
| ObjectKernel, registered after init | `warn` at init; 2 queries admitted, 2 reads | `info` at init; 2 queries admitted, 2 reads |
| LiteKernel, registered after init | `warn` at init; 2 admitted, 2 reads | `info` at init; 2 admitted, 2 reads |
| ObjectKernel, never registered | `warn` at init; per query `error` + 403, 0 reads | `info` at init; per query `error` + 403, 0 reads |
| LiteKernel, never registered | `warn` at init; per query `error` + 403, 0 reads | `info` at init; per query `error` + 403, 0 reads |

## Pins (`admission-absence-report.test.ts`)

1. Default composition on a real `LiteKernel`, security registered from `start()`: no admission `warn`/`error` at boot; the init line is the `info` above.
2. Same composition: the first query asks `canReadObject('employer_member', ctx)`; an admitted caller gets rows (1 read); a refusing service gives `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403 with 0 reads.
3. Real `LiteKernel`, no security service ever: no init-time admission WARN; the query is denied `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403, 0 reads, with the bridge's existing `error` line (unchanged outcome).
4. ABSENT resolution (context answers nothing): no WARN at init; the first query is admitted and WARNs once, naming `employer_member`; the second query is admitted and does not repeat it; no `error`.
5. Per plugin instance: two separate inits each get their own single report.

## Ablations (head `9c632fe74a`; mutation through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` with an anchor that must hit, an outer `trap` restore, and a blob-hash proof)

The subject is imported from source (`../plugin.js`), so no `dist` leg applies. Each leg: anchor x1 to x0, replacement x0 to x1, restored blob `fc1df493483a` equal to `HEAD:plugin.ts`, `git diff HEAD` empty.

- **A1**, the init line back to `ctx.logger.warn`: 6 failed / 8 passed; red on pins 1 to 5 and on `raw-sql-object-routing` "leaves default-datasource objects exactly where they were".
- **A2**, once-guard removed (`if (true)`): 1 failed / 13 passed; red on pin 4 (the second query repeats the WARN).
- **A3**, the query-time WARN demoted to `debug`: 3 failed / 11 passed; red on pins 4 and 5 and on the same `raw-sql-object-routing` case.

## Local verification (head `9c632fe74a`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-analytics build`: ok. `typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`, whose program includes the new test file): exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-analytics exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: Test Files 179 passed (179); Tests 4415 passed, 262 skipped (4677).
- Gates: the 64 families `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derives on `9c632fe74a`, plus `pnpm check:startup-registry-verdict` and `pnpm check:init-service-contract`: 66 of 66 exit 0. `dispatch-gates --ran`: 64 derived, 64 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
- Lint, narrowed: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 4 touched source files. The config lints every `*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}` outside its never-linted list and `packages/spec/**`, so all 4 are in scope; the JSON reports 4 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. The config never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any file it does not touch. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- When a host supplies `getReadScope` but not `admitObjectRead`, `securityPresentAtInit` is never probed, so the admission init line reads "not registered yet at init" even when a security service is present. Before this PR the same branch was a WARN. The line is now `info`; the condition is unchanged and is noted here, not changed.
- `analytics-service.ts:1901` (`assertReadAdmitted` doc) still says "`AnalyticsServicePlugin` reports that state at init." It is now reported at init at `info`, and at the first query at `warn`. That file is outside this card's file surface, so it is noted here, not edited.
- `check:startup-registry-verdict` cannot see init-time verdicts about a service its provider registers in `start()` (see H3).
